title: The Taliban Takeover, One Year Later

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上你都会带着300张你最珍贵的藏品去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个像是由精美50年历史艺术品组成的流动的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Ketrowa.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是娜塔莉·凯特罗瓦。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: One year ago this week, when the Taliban retook control of Afghanistan, it promised to institute a moderate form of Islamic government that honored women's rights.
sentences.zh: 一年前的本周，当塔利班重新夺回阿富汗控制权时，它承诺建立一种尊重妇女权利的温和形式的伊斯兰政府。

sentences.en: But that promise evaporated with its decision to prohibit young women from going to school.
sentences.zh: 但随着其禁止年轻女性上学的决定，这一承诺化为乌有。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Matthew Akins on what led to that decision, and what it reveals about which part of the Taliban is really running Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事马修·艾金斯将讲述是什么导致了这一决定，以及它揭示了塔利班的哪一部分在真正掌控阿富汗。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, August 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月16日，星期二。

sentences.en: Matt, you were in Afghanistan a year ago as the Taliban took over.
sentences.zh: 马特，一年前塔利班接管阿富汗时你正在那里。

sentences.en: Remind us what our expectations were at the time for how things might play out.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下我们当时对局势发展方向的预期是什么。

sentences.en: Well, I can remember last summer, as the previous Afghan government's forces started to collapse around the country as U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得去年夏天，随着美国军队撤出，前阿富汗政府的军队开始在全国各地崩溃，

sentences.en: troops withdrew, that there was this mounting sense of panic in Kabul, that the Taliban were going to come in,
sentences.zh: 喀布尔有一种不断加剧的恐慌情绪，认为塔利班将要进城，

sentences.en: they were going to arrest and kill people who had worked with the foreigners,
sentences.zh: 他们将逮捕和杀害那些与外国人合作过的人，

sentences.en: that there would be a return to the 90s where they were whipping women and men without beards in the streets, and that there would just be this bloodbath, this brutal repression.
sentences.zh: 90年代那种在街上鞭打妇女和不留胡须男性的情景将会重演，并且会出现一场血洗，一场残酷的镇压。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the Taliban were promising that they would not kill people if they surrendered, and that was a big factor behind their success.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，塔利班承诺如果人们投降就不会杀害他们，这是他们成功的一个重要因素。

sentences.en: That's why they were able to take so much territory so quickly.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们能够如此迅速地占领如此多的领土。

sentences.en: And that was one of the reasons why me and my housemate decided to stay and report on the fall of Kabul.
sentences.zh: 这也是我和室友决定留下来报道喀布尔陷落的原因之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember you came on the show, and you had interviewed the spokesman for the Taliban
sentences.zh: 我记得你曾上过这个节目，你采访了塔利班的发言人，

sentences.en: right after the takeover, and it sounded like he was trying to reassure you and maybe the world that all of those fears wouldn't actually come to pass.
sentences.zh: 就在接管后不久，听起来他试图让你乃至全世界放心，所有这些恐惧实际上都不会发生。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: I sat down with Zabiullah Mujahid, and he was trying to show a new face of the Taliban to the world.
sentences.zh: 我与扎比乌拉·穆贾希德进行了交谈，他试图向世界展现塔利班的新面孔。

sentences.en: And he promised that there would be this general amnesty, that the war was over, that people would be forgiven for the past,
sentences.zh: 他承诺将实行大赦，战争已经结束，人们过去的行为将被原谅，

sentences.en: and that there wouldn't be a return to that kind of violence that we'd seen in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 并且不会重演我们在90年代见过的那种暴力。

sentences.en: And he, in fact, promised that the emirate would be respecting people's rights.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他承诺酋长国将尊重人们的权利。

sentences.en: Okay, so he makes those promises, but what's actually playing out on the ground?
sentences.zh: 好的，所以他做出了这些承诺，但地面上的实际情况如何？

sentences.en: Well, I think it was a very mixed, uneasy situation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个非常复杂、令人不安的局面。

sentences.en: Everyone was kind of waiting to see what they would do.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在某种程度上等待着看他们会做什么。

sentences.en: And while there weren't massacres, there were people being arrested, journalists being beaten, there's allegations of people being killed.
sentences.zh: 虽然没有发生大屠杀，但有人被捕，记者被殴打，还有人被杀害的指控。

sentences.en: The more we heard these allegations, the more skeptical it made people that the Taliban had really changed.
sentences.zh: 我们听到这些指控越多，人们就越怀疑塔利班是否真的改变了。

sentences.en: But even skeptics of the Taliban, I think, acknowledged that the country had changed so much that the Taliban, in the very least, would be forced to deal with a new reality.
sentences.zh: 但即使是塔利班的怀疑论者，我认为也承认这个国家已经发生了很大变化，塔利班至少将被迫面对现实。

sentences.en: And, of course, one of the biggest changes since 2001 was that millions of Afghan girls have been allowed to go to school.
sentences.zh: 当然，自2001年以来最大的变化之一是，数百万阿富汗女孩被允许上学。

sentences.en: They've been educated.
sentences.zh: 她们受过教育。

sentences.en: Their families have seen the benefits of that education.
sentences.zh: 她们的家庭看到了这种教育的好处。

sentences.en: It's a big change in Afghan society.
sentences.zh: 这是阿富汗社会的巨大变化。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, after the collapse of the republic last August, all the schools were closed, boys and girls.
sentences.zh: 现在，在去年8月共和国崩溃后，所有的学校都关闭了，无论男女。

sentences.en: The next month, the Taliban reopened them.
sentences.zh: 第二个月，塔利班重新开放了学校。

sentences.en: But they didn't allow girls to go back to high school, just elementary.
sentences.zh: 但他们不允许女孩重返高中，只允许上小学。

sentences.en: And that, of course, stirred outrage, both within Afghanistan and among the international community.
sentences.zh: 当然，这在阿富汗国内和国际社会都引起了愤怒。

sentences.en: But the Taliban insisted that this was just temporary until they could get additional measures in place
sentences.zh: 但塔利班坚称这只是暂时的，直到他们能够采取额外措施，

sentences.en: so that men and women, boys and girls, didn't mix in a way that was at odds with their strict interpretation of Islam.
sentences.zh: 使得男女生在交往时不会违背他们对伊斯兰教的严格解释。

sentences.en: And so, as the first day of classes approached...
sentences.zh: 因此，随着开学第一天的临近……

sentences.en: Now, the Taliban in Afghanistan is due to lift its ban and allow girls to return to secondary school classroom...
sentences.zh: 现在，阿富汗的塔利班将解除禁令，允许女孩重返中学课堂……

sentences.en: We started hearing statements and even promises from the Taliban that teenage girls would finally be allowed to go back to school.
sentences.zh: 我们开始听到塔利班的声明甚至承诺，青少年女孩最终将被允许重返学校。

sentences.en: And it's also, you know, one of the demands of the international community for the Taliban to protect and safeguard the rights of girls and women to go to school.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这也是国际社会的要求之一，要求塔利班保护和维护女孩和妇女上学的权利。

sentences.en: They planned a ceremony in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 他们在喀布尔策划了一个仪式。

sentences.en: They'd invited the few ambassadors still remaining in the capital.
sentences.zh: 他们邀请了首都仅存的几位大使。

sentences.en: Now, this is what's coming from the leadership.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是来自领导层的声音。

sentences.en: But I think we really have to see on the ground whether in March we do see those schools opening up because they have been...
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们真的必须在实地看看，3月份我们是否真的看到这些学校开放，因为它们已经……

sentences.en: So on March 23rd, all these Afghan teenage girls wake up.
sentences.zh: 所以在3月23日，所有这些阿富汗女学生都醒了过来。

sentences.en: They put on their uniforms, went to class.
sentences.zh: 她们穿上制服，去上学。

sentences.en: For these students in the west of Kabul, returning to school felt particularly poignant.
sentences.zh: 对于喀布尔西部的这些学生来说，重返学校感觉特别辛酸。

sentences.en: Of course, the media showed up to cover these girls arriving at school.
sentences.zh: 当然，媒体赶来报道这些女孩抵达学校的情况。

sentences.en: Thank God, the Taliban are also like the previous government.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，塔利班也和上一届政府一样。

sentences.en: Now I don't have any concern about what I have to wear or whether to go to school or not.
sentences.zh: 现在我不用担心我该穿什么衣服，或者是否该去上学了。

sentences.en: My family has...
sentences.zh: 我的家庭已经……

sentences.en: Hopeful that they'll finally be allowed to continue their education.
sentences.zh: 满怀希望地认为她们终于被允许继续接受教育。

sentences.en: It was going to be a very hopeful day for the entire country.
sentences.zh: 这对于整个国家来说将是非常充满希望的一天。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, word went around that the schools aren't opening after all.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，有消息传出学校终究不会开放。

sentences.en: And the ones that were open closed down, and those girls had to go home.
sentences.zh: 那些已经开学的学校又关门了，那些女孩不得不回家。

sentences.en: I was outside the country at the time watching the news coverage of these girls being sent home from school in tears.
sentences.zh: 当时我在国外，看着这些女孩流着泪被送回家的电视新闻报道。

sentences.en: I feel really hopeless for my future.
sentences.zh: 我对自己的未来感到彻底绝望。

sentences.en: I don't see a bright future for myself.
sentences.zh: 我看不到自己有什么光明的未来。

sentences.en: It was heartbreaking, but also baffling.
sentences.zh: 这令人心碎，但也令人费解。

sentences.en: Why would the Taliban do this?
sentences.zh: 塔利班为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: You know, why announce the schools would reopen only to reverse themselves the last minute like this?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么要宣布学校重新开放，却在最后一刻像这样反悔？

sentences.en: In a way that's so damaging for the Taliban standing, not just with their own society,
sentences.zh: 这种方式极大地损害了塔利班的声誉，不仅仅是在他们自己的社会中，

sentences.en: but also with the international community who at this moment is scrambling to find billions of dollars to stave off a massive humanitarian catastrophe in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 而且在国际社会中也是如此，国际社会目前正在争先恐后地寻找数十亿美元，以避免阿富汗发生大规模的人道主义灾难。

sentences.en: Didn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Yeah, we covered this on the show.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在节目中报道过这一点。

sentences.en: The humanitarian disaster unfolding in Afghanistan has really only been kept at bay by all of this international money.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗正在上演的人道主义灾难实际上完全靠这些国际资金勉强维持着。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And so this sudden decision to keep girls' high schools closed put all of that at risk.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个突然决定让女子高中继续关闭，将这一切置于危险之中。

sentences.en: So I decided to go back to Afghanistan in order to find out why the Taliban had reversed course at the last minute with so much at stake.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定重返阿富汗，去查明为什么塔利班在事关重大时会在最后一刻改变方针。

sentences.en: I fly back to Kabul in May.
sentences.zh: 我在5月份飞回喀布尔。

sentences.en: Regular flights have resumed to Dubai and Islamabad.
sentences.zh: 飞往迪拜和伊斯兰堡的定期航班已经恢复。

sentences.en: And there's a new sign at the airport terminal.
sentences.zh: 机场航站楼有了一个新标牌。

sentences.en: The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan desires peaceful and positive relations with the world.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗伊斯兰酋长国渴望与世界建立和平与积极的关系。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And some life has returned to the streets of Kabul.
sentences.zh: 喀布尔的街道恢复了一些生气。

sentences.en: And so I went around to different ministries to talk to the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 于是我走访了不同的部委与塔利班交谈。

sentences.en: So what's it like inside those ministries?
sentences.zh: 那么这些部委内部是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, it's the same ministries, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然还是那些部委。

sentences.en: And many of the low and mid-level bureaucrats at the ministries are the same officials who served under the Republic.
sentences.zh: 部委里的许多中低层官僚都是曾在共和国政府任职的官员。

sentences.en: But instead of suits and ties, now they're wearing traditional robes.
sentences.zh: 但他们不再穿西装打领带，而是穿着传统的长袍。

sentences.en: You don't see a lot of women anymore.
sentences.zh: 你已经看不到多少女性了。

sentences.en: And in the offices, you know, their bosses are the Taliban appointees who are, for the most part, religiously trained men in turbans who are now in charge.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在办公室里，他们的老板是塔利班任命的人员，主要是受过宗教培训、戴着头巾的掌权男子。

sentences.en: So I went to the education ministry and I sat with a senior Taliban official who asked to remain anonymous because of how sensitive the issue was.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了教育部，与一位高级塔利班官员坐在一起，由于问题敏感，他要求保持匿名。

sentences.en: And I asked him, why weren't the Taliban allowing girls to go to high school?
sentences.zh: 我问他，为什么塔利班不允许女孩上高中？

sentences.en: Well, he was eager to point out that they were already allowing girls to go back to elementary school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他急忙指出他们已经允许女孩重返小学。

sentences.en: They were allowing women to go to university, girls to go to private high schools.
sentences.zh: 他们允许妇女上大学，女孩上私立高中。

sentences.en: And even in some rural areas, girls' attendance was up.
sentences.zh: 甚至在一些农村地区，女孩的出勤率也有所上升。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: It kind of sounds like he's saying that in some places, access to education for girls might actually be improving.
sentences.zh: 听起来他似乎在说，在某些地方，女孩获得教育的机会实际上可能正在改善。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering what he said about the decision to close the high schools for girls.
sentences.zh: 但我想知道他对关闭女孩高中的决定是怎么说的。

sentences.en: Well, he said something that I really wasn't expecting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他说了一些我完全没有预料到的话。

sentences.en: He said that he thought it was a complete mistake and that he was hoping they would reopen.
sentences.zh: 他说他认为这是一个彻底的错误，他希望学校能重新开放。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What was surprising was he wasn't the only one who told me that in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，在喀布尔对我说这话的不止他一个人。

sentences.en: I met with a lot of Taliban officials who were very frustrated by the decision to keep girls out of school.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了许多塔利班官员，他们对不让女孩上学的决定感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: Not only because they saw it as being against their own self-interest, but because, you know, they wanted their daughters to be educated.
sentences.zh: 不仅因为他们认为这违背了自身的利益，而且因为，你知道，他们希望自己的女儿受到教育。

sentences.en: It sounds like the view inside the Taliban is actually very similar to the view from outside, that girls should be going to school.
sentences.zh: 听起来塔利班内部的观点实际上与外部的观点非常相似，即女孩应该去上学。

sentences.en: Well, that was the view from Kabul, at least, where these officials had been preparing to bring girls back to school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少在喀布尔是这样，这些官员一直在准备让女孩重返学校。

sentences.en: But as the first day of class approached, they learned that this wasn't their decision to make.
sentences.zh: 但随着开学第一天的临近，他们得知这不是他们能做出的决定。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市DealBook峰会的现场舞台上采访商业、政治和文化领域的一些最具影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在NYTimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不想错过它。

sentences.en: Matt, if it wasn't government officials in Kabul who could decide whether to reopen schools, who could?
sentences.zh: 马特，如果喀布尔的政府官员无权决定是否重新开放学校，那谁可以？

sentences.en: So to understand how power works in the Taliban today, you have to look at their government in the 90s, when in addition to the formal government cabinet in Kabul,
sentences.zh: 因此，要理解今天塔利班的权力运作方式，你必须看看他们在90年代的政府，当时除了喀布尔的正式政府内阁之外，

sentences.en: you had a second, more powerful shadow government,
sentences.zh: 你还有一个第二个、更强大的影子政府，

sentences.en: 300 miles away from Kabul, in the southern city of Kandahar.
sentences.zh: 距离喀布尔300英里远的南部城市坎大哈。

sentences.en: That's where the Taliban first got started, and that's where their supreme leader, Mullah Muhammad Omar, lived.
sentences.zh: 那是塔利班最初发迹的地方，也是他们的最高领导人毛拉·穆罕默德·奥马尔居住的地方。

sentences.en: And he presided over a leadership council, the Shura, which operated on consensus.
sentences.zh: 他主持了一个协商一致的领导委员会——舒拉。

sentences.en: That was what led the insurgency over the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 这就是过去20年来领导叛乱的机构。

sentences.en: And when the Taliban suddenly captured power last year, this old structure was grafted onto the new government.
sentences.zh: 当塔利班去年突然夺取政权时，这个旧结构被嫁接到了新政府身上。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I learned on this trip was that it was still very much in charge.
sentences.zh: 我在这次旅行中了解到的事情之一是，它仍然在很大程度上掌权。

sentences.en: Even today, you're saying that you have one government in Kabul, and you have this entirely separate decision-making body in Kandahar.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，你是说喀布尔有一个政府，而坎大哈还有一个完全独立的决策机构。

sentences.en: How does that work exactly?
sentences.zh: 这到底是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Well, for the most part, the government in Kabul gets to run the day-to-day affairs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在大多数情况下，喀布尔的政府负责处理日常事务。

sentences.en: But really important issues have to be decided by the supreme leader, who's currently Sheikh Haibatullah Ahunzada, and his leadership shura.
sentences.zh: 但真正重要的问题必须由最高领导人（目前是谢赫·海巴图拉·阿洪扎达）和他的领导舒拉来决定。
zh_words: 谢赫·海巴图拉·阿洪扎达

sentences.en: And that's what happened with the girls' schools.
sentences.zh: 女校事件就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: The education minister and the rest of the cabinet, many of whom are also on this shura, were summoned to Kandahar for a meeting.
sentences.zh: 教育部长和内阁其他成员（其中许多人也在这个舒拉中）被召集到坎大哈开会。

sentences.en: And over the course of several days, where they also debated other issues, they just couldn't get to an agreement on the school's reopening.
sentences.zh: 在经过几天的会议期间，他们还辩论了其他问题，但就是无法就学校重新开放达成一致。

sentences.en: There were a number of hard-line clerics who couldn't be convinced, and if there was no consensus and no decision from the supreme leader, then the girls' schools wouldn't reopen.
sentences.zh: 有许多强硬派神职人员无法被说服，如果没有共识，也没有最高领导人的决定，那么女校就不会重新开放。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until 11 at night on the day before classes that the call came from Kandahar to the education ministry, and they were completely blindsided by it.
sentences.zh: 直到开学前一天的晚上11点，坎大哈才给教育部打来电话，他们对此完全感到措手不及。

sentences.en: Did this shadow government in Kandahar give any explanation for its decision?
sentences.zh: 坎大哈的这个影子政府对其决定做出了任何解释吗？

sentences.en: Well, the meetings, the shura, are off-limits to journalists.
sentences.zh: 嗯，会议和舒拉是对记者禁绝的。

sentences.en: And it's surprising how opaque some of this decision-making is.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，其中一些决策过程是如此不透明。

sentences.en: I found a lot of the Taliban that I spoke to were confused about the reasons and who was really behind this decision.
sentences.zh: 我发现我交谈过的许多塔利班成员都对原因以及谁真正幕后操纵这个决定感到困惑。

sentences.en: But basically, for the hardliners in Kandahar, the resistance to girls' education comes from this very traditional view of life in the village, where women don't leave the house.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，对坎大哈的强硬派来说，对女孩教育的抵抗来自于这种非常传统的乡村生活观点，即女性不离开家。

sentences.en: And not long after the closure of girls' high schools was upheld in March.
sentences.zh: 就在3月份维持关闭女子高中的决定不久后，

sentences.en: The Taliban came out with another very controversial decree saying that the Taliban has ordered that any woman going out in public will have to wear a burqa.
sentences.zh: 塔利班发布了另一个极具争议的法令，称塔利班已下令任何上街的女性都必须穿布卡罩袍。

sentences.en: Afghan women should cover their faces in public when they're around unmarried men and that they should either wear a full-face veil or, even better, a burqa.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗女性在公共场合靠近未婚男性时应该遮住脸，她们应该戴全脸面纱，或者更好的是穿布卡罩袍。

sentences.en: And that the best hijab of all is to not even leave the house.
sentences.zh: 而且最好的希贾布是不离开家。

sentences.en: This new rule is one of the most severe restrictions on women since the Taliban regained control last AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 这项新规定是自去年8月塔利班重新掌权以来对女性最严厉的限制之一。

sentences.en: So that feels like an escalation to me.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一种升级。

sentences.en: Like, the Taliban is making an even sharper turn toward a more conservative version of Islam.
sentences.zh: 就像塔利班正朝着更保守的伊斯兰教版本做出更急剧的转向。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: I think on one hand, it is kind of a sop to the hardliners, the traditionalists, who just want to see very strict rules against mixing between men and women implemented
sentences.zh: 我认为一方面，这有点像是在向强硬派和传统主义者示好，他们只想看到实施针对男女交往的非常严格的规则。

sentences.en: and would rather see women at home.
sentences.zh: 并且宁愿看到女性呆在家里。

sentences.en: But for others, including the education minister, who was one of the religious scholars who signed this decree, this is kind of setting the groundwork in theory
sentences.zh: 但对其他人来说，包括签署了这项法令的宗教学者之一、教育部长，这在理论上算是为

sentences.en: for girls to go back to class, for women to go back to offices, to have them veiled or separated from men.
sentences.zh: 女孩重返课堂、女性重返办公室奠定了基础，让她们戴上面纱或与男性隔离开来。

sentences.en: They say they want girls to work, but only if they are veiled when they're in public according to what they say are the principles of Islamic law.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们希望女孩工作，但前提是她们在公共场合时按照他们所说的伊斯兰教法原则戴上面纱。

sentences.en: So it sounds like they might have different reasons for it, but the moderates and the hardliners are both kind of in favor of this decree.
sentences.zh: 听起来他们对此可能有不同的原因，但温和派和强硬派都某种程度上支持这项法令。

sentences.en: On the level of religious ideology, yeah.
sentences.zh: 从宗教意识形态的层面上讲，是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was also surprising to me how many of the Taliban officials that I spoke to weren't happy with these decrees.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我也感到惊讶的是，我交谈过的许多塔利班官员对这些法令并不满意。

sentences.en: They didn't see it as pragmatic to focus on these kind of culture wars when they're trying to rebuild their country, they're trying to govern, they're trying to feed a population
sentences.zh: 当他们试图重建国家、试图执政、试图养活深陷

sentences.en: that's struggling with catastrophic levels of hunger.
sentences.zh: 灾难性饥饿水平的人口时，他们并不认为把精力集中在这一类文化战争上是务实的。

sentences.en: And, you know, as we discussed, one of the ways that people are being kept from starvation in Afghanistan is through international aid.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，正如我们所讨论的，阿富汗人免于挨饿的方式之一是通过国际援助。

sentences.en: And the largest donor to those aid efforts is the United States.
sentences.zh: 而这些援助工作最大的捐助国是美国。

sentences.en: And the Taliban has been working pragmatically with the U.S., with the international community to give access to aid groups on the ground.
sentences.zh: 塔利班一直在务实地与美国、与国际社会合作，为地面上的援助组织提供准入。

sentences.en: You know, over the winter, they were feeding half the population.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在冬天的时候，他们养活了一半的人口。

sentences.en: And so these kinds of provocative moves around veiling and the burqa and especially the girls' schools, that just makes all of that harder.
sentences.zh: 所以这些围绕面纱、布卡袍特别是女校的挑衅性举动，只会让这一切变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I wonder, Matt, if those more pragmatic voices within the Taliban government don't have a point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，马特，我在想，塔利班政府内部那些更务实的声音难道没有道理吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if Afghanistan is so dependent on international money, it seems unwise to piss off those donors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果阿富汗如此依赖国际资金，惹怒这些捐助者似乎是不明智的。

sentences.en: I mean, is there any more charged issue to throw in the face of the West than the issue of girls being able to go to school?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，还有什么比女孩能否上学这个问题更能激怒西方呢？

sentences.en: No, there's not.
sentences.zh: 不，没有了。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, it's quite provocative.
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，这相当具有挑衅性。

sentences.en: But, you know, on the other hand, I think the Taliban realize that the West is giving humanitarian aid to Afghanistan, not because of anything they do or don't do,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，另一方面，我认为塔利班意识到西方对阿富汗提供人道主义援助，不是因为他们做了或没做什么，

sentences.en: but because the West doesn't want to see Afghans starve.
sentences.zh: 而是因为西方不希望看到阿富汗人挨饿。

sentences.en: They don't want to see Afghans migrate to other countries and to Europe.
sentences.zh: 他们不想看到阿富汗人移民到其他国家和欧洲。

sentences.en: They don't want to see collapse in the country.
sentences.zh: 他们不想看到这个国家崩溃。

sentences.en: So in a sense, they're willing to call the West's bluff and govern their way in the knowledge that there will be humanitarian assistance.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，他们愿意叫板西方的虚张声势，并在明知会有国际人道主义援助的情况下继续执政。

sentences.en: So when you say the Taliban is calling the West's bluff, it's basically like you say you care about girls being able to go to school, about these social issues,
sentences.zh: 所以当你说是塔利班在叫板西方的虚张声势时，基本上就像你说你在乎女孩能否上学、在乎这些社会问题，

sentences.en: but are you really willing to cut off humanitarian aid if we move in the opposite direction?
sentences.zh: 但如果我们朝相反方向行事，你们真的愿意切断人道主义援助吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, I think a year out from the collapse of the Afghan Republic last summer, which had seemed like such a massive disaster, there is a kind of quiet satisfaction
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为在去年夏天阿富汗共和国崩溃（当时看起来像是一场巨大的灾难）一年之后，华盛顿和其他西方首都有一种

sentences.en: in Washington and other Western capitals that the crisis has been contained.
sentences.zh: 安静的满足感，认为危机已经得到了控制。

sentences.en: You know, you haven't had massive flows of refugees to Europe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，并没有出现大规模流向欧洲的难民潮。

sentences.en: You haven't had famine in the country.
sentences.zh: 这个国家也没有发生饥荒。

sentences.en: And part of that is because the Taliban has played a stabilizing role by cooperating with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于塔利班通过与美国

sentences.en: and humanitarian agencies.
sentences.zh: 和人道主义机构合作，发挥了稳定作用。

sentences.en: There aren't a lot of good options in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 在阿富汗，并没有太多好的选择。

sentences.en: And it seems to me that the Biden administration's strategy is, you know, as one U.S.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，拜登政府的策略是，正如一位美国

sentences.en: official described it, keep Afghanistan off the front page.
sentences.zh: 官员所描述的那样，让阿富汗远离头版。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国政府中的许多人

sentences.en: government would like to forget about Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 希望把阿富汗忘掉。

sentences.en: But there are certainly some things the Taliban have done that have provoked a response from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但塔利班所做的一些事情确实引发了美国的反应。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, we saw the other day when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们前几天看到，美国

sentences.en: targeted the leader of al-Qaeda with a drone strike in downtown Kabul, right by where he used to go jogging in the mornings.
sentences.zh: 在喀布尔市中心用无人机袭击了基地组织头目，地点就在他以前早起慢跑的地方附近。

sentences.en: He was living there in a house, apparently sheltered by the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 他当时住在那里的一所房子里，显然受到了塔利班的庇护。

sentences.en: And so this tells us that if Afghanistan again becomes a threat to the world and to its neighbors like it did in the 90s,
sentences.zh: 这告诉我们，如果阿富汗再次像90年代那样对世界及其邻国构成威胁，

sentences.en: then the world will intervene.
sentences.zh: 那么世界就会进行干预。

sentences.en: I mean, in other words, you can kind of imagine that there are actually some decisions from the Taliban that the United States
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，换句话说，你可以想象，实际上塔利班做出的一些决定是美国

sentences.en: and other Western countries aren't just going to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 和其他西方国家根本不会容忍的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that that's what the pragmatists in Kabul understand.
sentences.zh: 我认为喀布尔的务实派正是理解了这一点。

sentences.en: But the question is whether the hardliners in Kandahar do.
sentences.zh: 但问题坎大哈的强硬派是否也这样认为。

sentences.en: And what we've seen from the decision to keep Afghan high school girls out of class is it's those hardliners around the supreme leader who still hold power within the movement.
sentences.zh: 从不让阿富汗高中女生上学的决定中，我们看到，在运动内部仍然掌握权力的是最高领导人身边的那些强硬派。

sentences.en: But the Taliban is not a monolith.
sentences.zh: 但塔利班并非铁板一块。

sentences.en: And there is a process of coming to grips with the country that's happening right now.
sentences.zh: 而且目前正在经历一个正视这个国家现实的过程。

sentences.en: There is an internal debate.
sentences.zh: 内部存在辩论。

sentences.en: And ultimately, the reason why the Taliban should allow girls to go back to school is not because that's what the international community wants
sentences.zh: 归根结底，塔利班应该允许女孩重返学校，不是因为那是国际社会想要的，

sentences.en: or not because that's how they're going to get money from the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 也不是因为那是他们从西方获得资金的方式。

sentences.en: It's because it's the right thing to do for their country and for their daughters.
sentences.zh: 而是因为这对他们的国家和他们的女儿来说是正确的事情。

sentences.en: And that's what some of the people I spoke to in Kabul understand.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在喀布尔交谈过的一些人所理解的。

sentences.en: This is the demand of the majority of the Afghan population.
sentences.zh: 这是绝大多数阿富汗民众的要求。

sentences.en: Afghan girls and their families who've been demonstrating, who've been standing up for this.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗女孩和她们的家人一直在游行示威，一直在为之抗争。

sentences.en: We now know that there are divisions in the movement over this.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，运动内部在这个问题上存在分歧。

sentences.en: And that there's pragmatists in Kabul who want to move forward on this.
sentences.zh: 喀布尔有务实派希望在这个问题上取得进展。

sentences.en: But right now, it's the hardliners who have the power in Kandahar.
sentences.zh: 但目前在坎大哈掌握权力的是强硬派。

sentences.en: The question really is, is that going to stay that way?
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，这种情况会保持不变吗？

sentences.en: Or can it change going forward?
sentences.zh: 还是未来会有所改变？

sentences.en: Matt, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 马特，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app, unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能查阅所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间去突破付费墙，看看《时报》订户每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订户，请立即下载《时报》应用，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Prosecutors informed Rudy Giuliani that he was a target in a criminal investigation into election interference in Georgia, a sign of intensifying legal pressures
sentences.zh: 检察官通知鲁迪·朱利安尼，他是佐治亚州选举干预刑事调查的目标，这表明

sentences.en: on former President Donald Trump and his allies.
sentences.zh: 前总统唐纳德·特朗普及其盟友面临的法律压力正在加剧。

sentences.en: Identifying Giuliani as a target suggests that prosecutors think he could be indicted in the case based on the evidence they've seen.
sentences.zh: 将朱利安尼确定为目标表明，根据他们看到的证据，检察官认为他可能会在该案中被起诉。

sentences.en: The news came on the same day that a federal judge rejected efforts by another key Trump ally,
sentences.zh: 这一消息传出的同一天，一名联邦法官驳回了特朗普的另一位核心盟友——

sentences.en: Senator Lindsey Graham, to avoid giving testimony in the Georgia case.
sentences.zh: 参议员林赛·格雷厄姆——试图避免在佐治亚州案件中作证的努力。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, until this summer.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科制作，直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自诩为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场痛苦、混乱有时又令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格将为您讲述那些试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都市。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
